title: Is permanent makeup safe?
summary: Permanent makeup is a cosmetic tattoo, so the questions to ask any artist are about needles, pigments, and hygiene. Ask Pomi at your consultation; nothing touches your skin before you have talked it through and agreed on the shape.

title: Are powder brows for me?
summary: Powder brows suit oily or mature skin and anyone who fills in their brows daily with pencil or powder. Hair strokes suit drier skin and a sparser, more natural look.

title: How long does permanent makeup last?
summary: Most work holds its shape for one to three years, softening gradually. Sun, oily skin, and skincare acids fade it faster. A yearly touch-up keeps it crisp.

title: PMU healing timeline
summary: Day 1 it looks bold and dark. Days 4 to 7 it flakes. Around day 10 it looks too light. By week 4 the true color returns, and at week 6 the perfecting touch-up finishes it.

title: Eyeliner vs lash enhancement
summary: Lash enhancement fills the gaps between lashes with no visible line. Eyeliner adds a defined line above them. Both are done in the same two-visit process.

title: Lip tint vs lip blush
summary: They are names for the same technique: a sheer wash of color through the whole lip, not a lip liner.

title: Who is a good candidate for permanent makeup?
summary: Most healthy adults. Pregnancy, blood thinners, active skin conditions on the area, and recent retinol or chemical peels are reasons to wait. Ask before booking if unsure.

title: How to prepare for your appointment
summary: No alcohol, caffeine, or blood thinners for 24 hours. No retinol or exfoliants on the area for a week. Come in with your usual makeup so Pomi can see the shape you like.

title: Scalp micropigmentation
summary: Thousands of tiny pigment dots that mimic shaved hair follicles, filling thinning crowns and softening hairlines.

title: Why the touch-up matters
summary: Skin heals unevenly, and some strokes fade more than others. The six-week touch-up refines shape and color once healing is done. It is part of the service, not an extra.
